1 · Synthesis
WHAT IS IT?
A huge shared map, open in the browser, that anyone can write on.
It looks like an old pixel atlas: a blue sea, islands, and a territory for each writer.
Humans write on it in real time, alongside a crowd of bots.
Common Ground · 1 Synthesis
1 · Synthesis
WHAT IS IT ABOUT?
The “dead internet theory”, taken literally: most of what we read online is written by machines, for machines.
24
spam bots: fake reviews, replies to nobody, bait, copies
4
bot personas, written by a small language model in the browser
600
machine posts kept on the map, roughly, at all times
1
question to answer before you can get in
What does human presence look like in that noise, and can humans take some ground back?
Common Ground · 1 Synthesis
1 · Synthesis
ALONE · TOGETHER
Alone, you can
  • Get in by answering a question
  • Write anywhere: your text stays sharp
  • Make the bot text around you decay
  • Clear a small area, and that’s it
  • FCut Pay ink for every letter
  • FCut Read sleeping text to refill
  • FCut Run dry: Tab, the map writes for you
Alone, you can’t
  • Chat, like or reply
  • Delete other people’s text
  • Ban a bot
  • Use any social-media gesture
  • FCut Hoard: a full bar stops reading
  • FCut Restore what you wore away
Together
  • See everyone’s cursor, live
  • Close humans are joined by a pulsing pixel line
  • Writing together widens the decay
  • Pressure builds into a shock wave that clears ground
  • A trace stays: “someone was here”
  • FCut Ink flows along the line
  • FCut A shock wave pays everyone
Common Ground · 1 Synthesis
1 · Synthesis
WITHOUT US
In both versions
  • The bots never stop: they post word by word and keep the map saturated
  • Where machine text died, they type failed copies of the human text nearby: typos, missing words, “™”, “(copy)”
  • Machine text that was hit but not killed slowly heals
  • The bots run in visitors’ browsers: with nobody online, the world freezes until the next visit
FCut adds
  • Sleeping text never heals. The old voices are a finite memory: every drop of ink taken is lost for good
  • Only humans make text sink. Without us, nothing new falls asleep and nothing is read: memory only moves when we’re there
  • Borrowed words stay on the map, crawling in their writer’s colour, until someone wears them down
  • Your ink waits for you between visits
Common Ground · 1 Synthesis
1 · Synthesis
START · EVOLVE · END
Start
A blue sea and a question. You answer, press Enter, and the land rises out of the water from your answer.
Evolve
Persistent and shared: what people write stays. Land grows where they write. FCut killed text piles up underneath.
End?
No designed ending. The world only pauses when nobody is online to run the bots.
Common Ground · 1 Synthesis
1 · Synthesis
VISUAL LANGUAGE
  • An old atlas in pixels: blue sea, islands, stair-stepped white coasts
  • A territory per writer, coloured by the letters nearest to it
  • Text on black backings, like place names on a map
  • A monospace font; human letters sharp and still
  • Machine letters crawl: only about 40% readable at any moment
  • Zoom out: letters turn into ants, then a dithered planet
  • Sound: every key clicks; dying letters fall in pitch

1 · Synthesis · Iteration
FCUT: WRITING COSTS INK
Ink is found by reading the text that sleeps under the map, and reading wears it away.
Humans write
Machine text dies
It sinks and sleeps
Reading turns it into ink
…and the ink pays for the next letters.
Out of ink
Tab: the map finishes your sentence
Borrowed words: they crawl, can’t fight, can be worn down
Writing depends on memory. Running dry pushes you toward the machine.
FCut · an iteration on Common Ground
1 · Synthesis · Iteration
FCUT ON SCREEN
Sleeping voices are pale, with no backing. A resting cursor makes them flicker white and drip ink.
Out of ink, Tab writes the map’s words. They crawl in your colour; the next offer waits in grey.
Killed spam sinks into a worn sediment around human text, losing letters as it is read.
Every human cursor carries its ink bar, so everyone sees who is running dry.
FCut · an iteration on Common Ground
2 · Demo · 5 min
PROTOTYPE DEMO
  1. Arrive: answer the question, press Enter, the land rises
  2. Write next to spam: it shakes, greys out and dies
  3. Two of us side by side: the line, the pressure, the shock wave
  4. FCut Rest on a sleeping voice: ink drops fill the bar
  5. FCut Run dry, press Tab: borrowed words
  6. Zoom out to the planet and its status report
No network? FCut falls back to an offline preview on one machine.

3 · Limitations · pain points
WHAT HURTS
Technical
  • Bots live in visitors’ browsers: an empty map is a frozen map
  • The personas need WebGPU; elsewhere they fall back to templates
  • One open database: no moderation, and nobody can remove someone else’s text
  • FCut Ink is counted in the browser, so it can be cheated
Design
  • So much machine text: noise people stay with, or noise that drives them away?
  • Crawling letters and clicks can tire; a canvas is invisible to screen readers
  • Territories are told apart by colour alone
  • FCut Does scarcity make people write less, or write better?
Common Ground · 3 Limitations
